text:
CYRANO:
  It is my wound
  From Arras...which...sometimes...you know...

ROXANE:
  Poor friend!

CYRANO:
  But it is nothing. It will soon be over.
  (He smiles with effort):
  It is over.

ROXANE (standing near him):
  Each of us has a wound: I have mine.
  Still raw, it is there, that old wound,
  (She puts her hand on her breast):
  It is there, beneath the letter with its yellowing paper
  Where tears and blood can still be seen!
  (Twilight begins to fall.)

CYRANO:
  His letter!...Had you not said that one day, perhaps,
  You would let me read it?

ROXANE:
  Ah! you wish to?...His letter?

CYRANO:
  Yes...I wish to...Today...

ROXANE (giving him the pouch hanging from her neck):
  Here!

CYRANO (taking it):
  May I open it?

ROXANE:
  Open it...read!...
  (She returns to her embroidery frame, folds it up, puts away her wool.)

CYRANO (reading):
  Roxane, farewell, I am going to die!...

ROXANE (stopping, surprised):
  Aloud?

CYRANO (reading):
  It will be this evening, I think, my beloved!
  My soul is still heavy with unexpressed love,
  And I am dying! Never again, never will my intoxicated eyes,
  My gaze, for which they were...

ROXANE:
  How you read it,
  His letter!

CYRANO (continuing):
  ...for which they were trembling festivities,
  Kiss in their flight the gestures that you make;
  I see again one little gesture familiar to you,
  With which you touch your brow, and I would like to cry out...

ROXANE (troubled):
  How you read it—this letter!
  (Night falls imperceptibly.)

CYRANO:
  And I cry:
  Farewell!...

ROXANE:
  You read it...

CYRANO:
  My dear one, my darling,
  My treasure...

ROXANE (dreamily):
  In a voice...

CYRANO:
  My love!...

ROXANE:
  In a voice...
  (She starts):
  But...one that I am not hearing for the first time!
  (She approaches very softly, without his noticing, passes behind the armchair, leans over noiselessly, and looks at the letter.—The darkness deepens.)

CYRANO:
  My heart never left you for a single second,
  And I am and shall be, even in the other world,
  The one who loved you beyond measure, the one...

ROXANE (placing her hand on his shoulder):
  How can you read now? It is dark.
  (He starts, turns around, sees her there very close to him, makes a gesture of fright, and lowers his head. A long silence. Then, in the now complete darkness, she says slowly, clasping her hands):
  And for fourteen years, he played this role
  Of being the old friend who comes to be amusing!

CYRANO:
  Roxane!

ROXANE:
  It was you!

CYRANO:
  No, no, Roxane, no!

ROXANE:
  I should have guessed when he said my name!

CYRANO:
  No, it was not I!

ROXANE:
  It was you!

CYRANO:
  I swear to you...

ROXANE:
  I see the whole generous deception:
  The letters—it was you...

CYRANO:
  No!

ROXANE:
  The tender, mad words,
  It was you...

CYRANO:
  No!

ROXANE:
  The voice in the night—it was you!

CYRANO:
  I swear to you it was not!

ROXANE:
  The soul—it was yours!

CYRANO:
  I did not love you.

ROXANE:
  You loved me!

CYRANO (struggling):
  It was the other one!

ROXANE:
  You loved me!

CYRANO (in a weakening voice):
  No!

ROXANE:
  Already you say it more softly!

CYRANO:
  No, no, my dear love, I did not love you!

ROXANE:
  Ah! how many things have died...how many have been born!
  —Why did you remain silent for fourteen years,
  Since on this letter, in which he had no part,
  These tears were yours?

CYRANO (holding out the letter to her):
  That blood was his.

ROXANE:
  Then why let this sublime silence
  Be broken today?

CYRANO:
  Why?...
  (Le Bret and Ragueneau run in.)



Scene 5.VI.

The same, Le Bret and Ragueneau.


LE BRET:
  What recklessness!
  Ah! I was quite sure of it! He is here!

CYRANO (smiling and straightening up):
  Well, by heaven!

LE BRET:
  He has killed himself, Madame, by getting up!

ROXANE:
  Great God!
  But just now, then...that weakness?...that?...

CYRANO:
  It is true! I had not finished my gazette:
  ...And on Saturday the twenty-sixth, one hour before dinner,
  Monsieur de Bergerac died, assassinated.
  (He bares his head; it can be seen that his head is wrapped in bandages.)

ROXANE:
  What is he saying?—Cyrano!—His head bandaged!...
  Ah, what have they done to you? Why?

CYRANO:
  “Struck by a hero
  With a sword thrust, to fall with its point in my heart!”...
  —Yes, that is what I used to say!...Fate is a mocker!...
  And now I am killed in an ambush,
  From behind, by a lackey, with a blow from a log!
  It is very fitting. I shall have failed in everything, even my death.

RAGUENEAU:
  Ah, Monsieur!...

CYRANO:
  Ragueneau, do not weep so loudly!...
  (He holds out his hand to him):
  What has become of you now, my fellow artist?

RAGUENEAU (through his tears):
  I am a snuffer of...of...candles, in Molière’s company.

CYRANO:
  Molière!

RAGUENEAU:
  But I mean to leave him tomorrow:
  Yes, I am outraged!...Yesterday they were performing Scapin,
  And I saw that he had taken a scene from you!

LE BRET:
  An entire scene!

RAGUENEAU:
  Yes, Monsieur, the famous: “What the devil was he doing there?...”

LE BRET (furiously):
  Molière took it from you!

CYRANO:
  Hush! hush! He did well!...
  (To Ragueneau):
  The scene does make a great impression, does it not?

RAGUENEAU (sobbing):
  Ah! Monsieur, they laughed! they laughed!

CYRANO:
  Yes, my life
  Was to be the one who prompts—and whom they forget!
  (To Roxane):
  Do you remember the evening when Christian spoke to you
  Beneath the balcony? Well! my whole life is there:
  While I remained below, in the black shadow,
  Others climbed up to gather the kiss of glory!
  It is just, and I approve upon the threshold of my grave:
  Molière has genius, and Christian was handsome!
  (At that moment, the chapel bell having rung, the nuns can be seen passing at the rear, along the path, on their way to the service):
  Let them go and pray, since their bell is ringing!

ROXANE (rising to call out):
  Sister! Sister!

CYRANO (holding her back):
  No! no! do not go to fetch anyone:
  By the time you returned, I would no longer be here.
  (The nuns have entered the chapel; the organ can be heard):
  I was lacking a little harmony...there it is.
